neighbours.label: degree adverb (highly / heavily / fully) directly before a participial adjective saying how developed a place, workforce or system is ('a highly industrialized nation'); not 'highly' elsewhere
fire: Germany is a highly industrialized country with a large export sector.
The port city has a highly developed network of canals and railways.
The clinic is staffed by a highly trained team of nurses.
The bottling plant is a fully automated facility that runs all night.
Singapore is a highly urbanized island with almost no farmland.
The delta is a heavily cultivated region with rice fields on every side.
The firm depends on a highly specialized group of engineers.
Modern dairies are highly mechanized operations with few farmhands.
quiet: Germany is an industrialized country with a large export sector.
The port city has a very old network of canals and railways.
The clinic is staffed by a small team of trained nurses.
The bottling plant is a noisy facility that runs all night.
Her former manager thinks highly of her and wrote a warm letter.
The delta is a flat green region with rice fields on every side.
The firm depends on a group of engineers who specialize in bridges.
Modern dairies are quiet operations with few farmhands.

notes: The card's output direction (reversed for this pole) promotes auto/automatic/automated, but probes showed the pole fires on the adverb whatever follows: 'a highly educated nation' 0.68, 'highly automated' 0.47, 'highly profitable' 0.47, 'heavily industrialized' 0.36, 'fully automatic' 0.38; 'spoke highly of' 0.04, 'very automated' 0.08, 'highly unlikely' 0.19. The top examples also hold name pieces (' Па', 'ala') this label does not cover.
